subject: Agriculture
title: Coffee Rust in Ceylon
description: A quick, practical guide to Coffee Rust in Ceylon.

hook.text: Ceylon (Sri Lanka) was the world's top coffee exporter in 1870. Within 20 years, not a single coffee tree remained.

buildup.text: Coffee rust fungus—Hemileia vastatrix—appeared in 1869, producing orange spores under every leaf.

discovery.text: The fungus blocked photosynthesis. Trees defoliated, stopped producing berries, and died within a few seasons.

twist.text: Planters ripped out coffee and planted tea instead. That's why Sri Lanka is famous for tea, not coffee.

climax.text: Coffee rust is still the most damaging coffee disease worldwide—costing $1 billion annually in Latin America.

punchline.text: A fungus turned a coffee island into a tea island. Disease rewrites economies.

quiz.question: Why did Sri Lanka switch from coffee to tea production?
options: Coffee rust destroyed all coffee trees, forcing planters to switch
